title: Sums and truncations in $\Dic(X,\Lambda)$; the localizing closure
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$. Let $X$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme, in the standing setting of [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $\Qlb$ be an algebraic closure of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and $E\subseteq\Qlb$ a finite extension of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$, with the condensed coefficient conventions of [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring; sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed], and put $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. All sheaves below are $\Lambda_X$-module objects [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Write $\mathcal A=\Mod_{\Lambda_X}$ and $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)=D(\mathcal A)$ for the ordinary unbounded derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. All families and filtered diagrams are small in the fixed universe of the site and coefficient sheaves.

Write $\Cons(X,\Lambda)$ for the constructible sheaves [sk-def-sfb-constructible] and $\IndCons(X,\Lambda)$ for the full subcategory of $\mathcal A$ consisting of filtered colimits of constructible sheaves, computed in $\mathcal A$. Set
$$\Dic(X,\Lambda)=\{K\in D(\mathcal A):H^n(K)\in\IndCons(X,\Lambda)\text{ for every }n\in\mathbf Z\}.$$
Write $\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$ for the bounded complexes with constructible cohomology [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible] and $\Loc(\mathcal S)$ for the smallest full triangulated subcategory containing $\mathcal S$ and closed under isomorphisms and arbitrary small direct sums [det-def-localizing-closure-existence]. For a representative complex $C$, the canonical truncation $\tau_{\le n}C$ has terms $C^i$ for $i<n$, $\ker d^n$ in degree $n$, and zero above $n$; $\tau_{\ge n}C$ has zero terms below $n$, $\operatorname{coker}d^{n-1}$ in degree $n$, and $C^i$ above $n$, with the induced differentials.

1. For any family $(K_s)$ in $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ and every $n\in\mathbf Z$, the canonical map
$$\bigoplus_s H^n(K_s)\longrightarrow H^n\!\left(\bigoplus_sK_s\right)$$
is an isomorphism. Consequently $\Dic(X,\Lambda)$ is closed under direct sums.
2. For $K\in\Dic(X,\Lambda)$ and $n\in\mathbf Z$, both $\tau_{\le n}K$ and $\tau_{\ge n}K$ lie in $\Dic(X,\Lambda)$.
3. $\Dbc(X,\Lambda)\subseteq\Dic(X,\Lambda)$ and $\Loc(\Dbc(X,\Lambda))\subseteq\Dic(X,\Lambda)$.

proof.text: The internal module category is Grothendieck abelian by the existing module-object Grothendieck instance (lem-sfb-modobj-grothendieck). Its small colimits exist, AB4 makes coproducts exact, and Grothendieck K-injective resolutions exist. Apply the proved source-library instance DerivedCategory.preservesColimitsOfShape_homologyFunctor. Given the arbitrary coproduct cocone c and cohomology cocone d of the statement, isColimitOfPreserves makes H^n(c) colimiting. IsColimit.nonempty_isColimit_iff_isIso_desc proves invertibility of exactly the specified canonical desc map. No boundedness or nonempty-index assumption is used.

Apply the sum clause of det-ind-heart-filtered-colimits to the cofan whose vertex is H^n(c.pt) and whose legs are H^n(c.inj i). Preservation from step 1 gives its colimit property. The assumed cohomology condition on each summand supplies every premise, proving sum closure of Dic. The empty family and the zero vertex give ContainsZero for the IndCons predicate; colimit universality follows from the unique maps out of zero.

ObjectProperty.ind is closed under isomorphisms. Apply the proved source-library lemmas DerivedCategory.homologyProperty_truncLE and DerivedCategory.homologyProperty_truncGE to the IndCons predicate, with ContainsZero from step 2. These lemmas compute surviving cohomology by the canonical truncation maps and use vanishing in the other degrees. This proves both truncation clauses for every integer cutoff.

Unfold constantModelBoundedConstructible only to obtain constructibility of every cohomology object. ObjectProperty.le_ind views each constructible object as its own filtered colimit over the one-object category, giving Dbc contained in Dic.

Use the triangulated clause of det-ambient-ind-derived-triangulated for Dic. Repleteness is inherited from ObjectProperty.ind under all homology functors. To meet the larger-index convention in sk-def-localizing-closure, inject the nonzero summands of any existing coproduct into its endomorphisms by their coordinate idempotents. For distinct indices these idempotents differ: composing with the first injection and its retraction gives an identity on one side and zero on the other. Thus locally small Homs make the nonzero support small in the coefficient universe. Remove zero summands using their unique maps, then shrink that support by equivShrink. The original coproduct remains the colimit of this small cofan. Apply step 2 to prove closure under every existing coproduct. Dic is therefore an IsLocalizingSubcategory. Evaluate the defining intersection localizingClosure at Dic and use step 4 to obtain Loc(Dbc) contained in Dic. Run these steps separately for the two coefficient rings, using the bottom finite subextension only to instantiate the unused finite-coefficient binder of the algebraic-closure triangulated clause.

proof_origin.place: Proof (1)-(3), realized using the proved HomologyCoproducts and HomologyProperty APIs; the nonzero-support universe argument is the existing LocalizingClosureExistence proof-plan step 4.

The latter states the standing-scheme restriction, and sk-def-sfb-dc-setting specifies separated finite-type schemes over a field of positive characteristic different from ell. The now-recorded ind-heart and ambient-triangulated interfaces have exactly that scope, with the ind-heart correction explicitly flagging this item as a breaking citer. Restore those source hypotheses rather than silently add them only in Lean. The parent unit already has that implicit standing setting; its conclusions and proof route are unchanged. No counterexample to the scoped assertion is claimed.
